latest.title: Jacobs appointed as Engineering/Regulatory Partner
latest.content:

EnergyPathways plc
("EnergyPathways" or the "Company")
Jacobs appointed as Tier-1 Engineering & Regulatory Partner
Jacobs appointed as strategic engineering and regulatory partner for EnergyPathways' MESH Long Duration Energy Storage project ("MESH")
EnergyPathways (AIM:EPP), the energy transition company, has selected Jacobs (NYSE:J) to provide planning, regulatory, consenting and environmental services for its proposed LDES project in the Irish Sea and Barrow-in-Furness. This includes assisting the Company in its submission to Ofgem's forthcoming Long Duration Energy Storage Cap and Floor round.
MESH, designated as a project of national significance by the UK Government, is positioned to become the UK's largest long-duration energy storage ("LDES") project at 300MW / 55 GWh / 100+hours duration. EnergyPathways' bespoke design is expected to provide substantial "total system benefits" to the UK's electricity grid.
Key highlights of the MESH LDES project:
·
Storage capability of several days versus only a handful of hours with batteries, enables it to store the increasing amounts of surplus UK wind power and reduce curtailment costs,
·
Lowering consumer power bills by providing lower run marginal cost dispatchable power vs traditional gas-fired power generation which often sets the price of the UK's electricity,
·
One of the lowest CAPEX per MWh of storage capacity providing significant value for taxpayer money versus other storage technologies, and
·
Strengthens grid resilience with synchronous inertia supply, fast response balancing power and reserve capacity to shore up national energy security.
Jacobs will provide strategic planning, consent support and leadership to key regulatory and planning activities to advance project approvals. This includes assisting the Company in Ofgem's forthcoming Cap and Floor round, a mechanism for providing approved LDES projects with a revenue floor sovereign guarantee enabling both private debt and equity investment in project development. Following the Company's submission to Ofgem, the next key milestone will be formal confirmation of MESH's eligibility in the Cap and Floor scheme.
Jacobs' work will include developing a stakeholder engagement plan covering local council and regional government and a grid connection application, as well as other workstreams required for the Cap and Floor round and for a government Development Consent Order (DCO) submission which will run in parallel. Jacobs will be engaged in work scopes including, but not limited to, statutory stakeholder engagement, socio-economic and regional employment and supply chain assessments to help inform project planning and community consideration.
Further announcements on Ofgem's Cap and Floor scheme will be made as soon as the next round has been declared open and the Company has made its formal submission.
Ben Clube, CEO of EnergyPathways, said:
"We are delighted that Jacobs will be joining the MESH project team and working alongside our Tier-1 partner group. Jacobs' extensive experience in other nationally significant government-led infrastructure and energy projects within the UK and their direct experience in delivering complex engineering projects in the Northwest of England will be invaluable as we take MESH forward.
"The planning and regulatory process that Jacobs will oversee will feed into our key submission under Ofgem's Cap and Floor scheme, which in turn, will underpin the Final Investment Decision of MESH. Successful eligibility in the Cap and Floor scheme offers a sovereign revenue guarantee that will significantly de-risk MESH and make it a highly bankable infrastructure asset for both debt and equity financing.
Jacobs' Executive Vice President Richard Sanderson said:
"As the UK accelerates investment in nationally significant energy infrastructure, successful delivery depends on a consenting strategy that integrates environmental stewardship and robust regulatory planning. MESH represents an important infrastructure development for Barrow-in-Furness and the wider UK energy system. Our extensive experience delivering complex infrastructure projects through the Development Consent Order process will support EnergyPathways in navigating planning and regulatory requirements while maintaining project momentum."

Issue of fee shares
EnergyPathways plc (AIM: EPP), an integrated energy transition company, announces the
issue of 875,054 new ordinary shares of 1 pence each
at
("Fee Shares")
in settlement of consultancy and advisory fees for members of the MESH project management team for Q2 2026.
Pursuant to the terms of the agreements with certain of the Company's directors and consultants, monthly fees are settled through a combination of cash payments and the periodic issue of new shares. Accordingly, the Company has issued 875,054 Fee Shares, representing a total of £61,509.20 in fees payable by the Company at a price of approximately 7.03 per Fee Share. The pricing for these shares is based on the 5-day VWAP for the last five days of trading, calculated on a monthly basis or current basis, as required under the contracts.
Admission and Total Voting Rights
Application will be made for the Fee Shares to be admitted to trading on AIM, which is expected to occur on or around 28 August 2026 ("Admission"). The Fee Shares will rank
pari passu
in all respects with the Company's existing ordinary shares currently traded on AIM.
Following Admission, the Company's issued share capital will comprise 251,700,216 ordinary shares of 1 pence each. This number will represent the total voting rights in the Company and may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculation by which they can determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the Company under the Financial Conduct Authority's Disclosure and Transparency Rules.

company_30s.what_they_do: EPP is a UK‑based renewable‑energy developer that builds and runs large‑scale energy‑storage and grid‑support projects, often in partnership with utilities and industrial players.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company sits at the heart of the transition to low‑carbon grids. With the UK’s push for more flexible storage to accommodate wind and solar, projects like EPP’s can unlock stranded renewable capacity and help utilities meet demand peaks.
company_30s.current_state: EPP has recently secured a key Ofgem LDES licence and drawn down financing for its MESH storage project. Governance has been refreshed with new directors and a chief scientific adviser, signalling a shift toward scaling operations. The firm is still in a growth‑phase, with limited revenue but growing capital commitments.

rns_narrative: EPP is tightening its regulatory footing: it won a new Ofgem LDES licence and is finalising the financing for its MESH storage facility, a critical step toward commercial deployment.
Governance is being modernised: appointments of independent directors and a chief scientific adviser are meant to strengthen oversight and technical expertise.
Corporate governance and shareholder rights are being clarified through AGM outcomes and voting‑rights disclosures, setting the stage for a more transparent capital structure.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – traders are largely silent but a few bullish voices see a potential breakthrough.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls highlight the Siemens partnership, the Ofgem licence, and the MESH drawdown as signs that the company is moving from concept to cash‑flow. They expect a sharp rebound when these milestones are announced.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the firm still has no revenue, relies heavily on external funding, and faces regulatory uncertainty. They fear a continued decline if the Ofgem cap does not materialise or if the MESH project stalls.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has stayed low, but the few bullish comments are growing stronger as the company hits key regulatory milestones.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat, signalling that the market has largely ignored EPP. This creates a surprise window if a catalyst hits.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the MESH financing drawdown – a clear sign that the project is moving forward.
Official announcement of the Ofgem LDES cap and floor – this could unlock a new revenue stream for storage operators.
Any public statement from Siemens confirming a partnership or technology transfer.
Results of the upcoming AGM – particularly any vote on new capital or strategic direction.
expect_next.watch_for: A sudden spike in trading volume, a breakout above the 52‑week low, or a sharp positive earnings or partnership announcement. A confirmation of the Ofgem licence in a press release would also be a green flag.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock sits in the early capitulation phase: a deep crash has already taken place, the APEX score indicates tight compression, and the lack of social chatter suggests the market is still waiting for a catalyst. If the next milestone arrives, a mean‑reversion bounce is likely to begin.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock is deeply discounted (likely >70% below its peak). Historically, RED and GREEN signals – the type we suspect here – have delivered 40–160% returns when a catalyst triggers a bounce. If the company clears the Ofgem licence and MESH drawdown, the price could climb to the midpoint of its 52‑week range, representing a 150–250% upside. The asymmetry is clear: the downside is capped at today’s price, while the upside is potentially several times that.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The firm remains pre‑revenue and depends on external funding. If the Ofgem cap fails to materialise or the MESH project stalls, the price could slide further into a deeper trough. A realistic worst‑case scenario would be a 10–15% drop from the current level if investor confidence evaporates.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential reward 2–3× the risk. With a 1‑unit risk at current price, upside could be 2–3 units if the company reaches the midpoint of its 52‑week range.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a bounce from the 52‑week low or a breakout above the recent resistance once the Ofgem or MESH news is confirmed. Use a stop 2–3% below the entry point to protect against a false move. Allocate 5–10% of portfolio per trade and adjust position size if volatility spikes.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until you see a volume spike of at least 50% over the 20‑day average and a price break above the 20‑day moving average. These are classic signs that the market is ready to reverse.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks at this stage.

ai_insights.bottom_line: EPP sits at a regulatory and financing crossroads; if the Ofgem licence and MESH drawdown materialise, a deep‑crashed, trend‑dead energy‑storage play could deliver a 150–250% upside while keeping downside limited to today’s price.
